1	---
2	title: cacheComponents
3	description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js.
4	related:
5	  links:
6	    - app/getting-started/caching
7	    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
8	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
9	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote
10	---
11	
12	Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
13	
14	## Usage
15	
16	To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file:
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
19	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
22	  cacheComponents: true,
23	}
24	
25	export default nextConfig
26	```
27	
28	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
29	
30	- The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
31	- The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
32	- The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
33	
34	> **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).
35	
36	Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.
37	
38	Read [How rendering works](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#how-rendering-works) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.
39	
40	> **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.
41	
42	## Navigation with Activity
43	
44	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.
45	
46	Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:
47	
48	- Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
49	- When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
50	- Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again
51	
52	This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.
53	
54	> **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.
55	
56	Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing.
57	
58	## Version History
59	
60	| Version | Change                                                                                                                            |
61	| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
62	| 16.0.0  | `cacheComponents` introduced. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. |
63

See docs/01-app/02-guides/instant-navigation.mdx */} 15 16 > This page covers caching with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide. 17 18 Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again. 19 20 ## Enabling Cache Components 21 22 You can enable Cache Components by adding the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your Next config file: 23 24 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4} switcher 25 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 26 27 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 28 cacheComponents: true, 29 } 30 31 export default nextConfig 32 ``` 33 34 ```js filename="next.config.js" highlight={3} switcher 35 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 36 const nextConfig = { 37 cacheComponents: true, 38 } 39 40 module.exports = nextConfig 41 ``` 42 43 > **Good to know:** When Cache Components is enabled, `GET` Route Handlers follow the same prerendering model as pages. See [Route Handlers with Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers#with-cache-components) for details. 44 45 ## Usage 46 47 The [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive caches the return value of async functions and components. You can apply it at two levels: 48 49 - **Data-level**: Cache a function that fetches or computes data (e.g., `getProducts()`, `getUser(id)`) 50 - **UI-level**: Cache an entire component or page (e.g., `async function BlogPosts()`) 51 52 > Arguments and any closed-over values from parent scopes automatically become part of the [cache key](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-keys), which means different inputs will produce separate cache entries. This enables personalized or parameterized cached content. See [serialization requirements and constraints](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#constraints) for details on what can be cached and how arguments work. 53 54 ### Data-level caching 55 56 To cache an asynchronous function that fetches data, add the `use cache` directive at the top of the function body: 57 58 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={3,4,5} 59 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 60 61 export async function getUsers() { 62 'use cache' 63 cacheLife('hours') 64 return db.query('SELECT * FROM users') 65 } 66 ``` 67 68 Data-level caching is useful when the same data is used across multiple components, or when you want to cache the data independently from the UI. 69 70 ### UI-level caching 71 72 To cache an entire component, page, or layout, add the `use cache` directive at the top of the component or page body: 73 74 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={1,4,5} 75 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 76 77 export default async function Page() { 78 'use cache' 79 cacheLife('hours') 80 81 const users = await db.query('SELECT * FROM users') 82 83 return ( 84
    85 {users.map((user) => ( 86
  • {user.name}
    • 87 ))} 88
89 ) 90 } 91 ``` 92 93 > If you add "`use cache`" at the top of a file, all exported functions in the file will be cached. 94 95 ### Streaming uncached data 96 97 For components that fetch data from an asynchronous source such as an API, a database, or any other async operation, and require fresh data on every request, do not use `"use cache"`. 98 99 Instead, wrap the component in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) and provide a fallback UI. At request time, React renders the fallback first, then streams in the resolved content once the async work completes. 100 101 ```tsx filename="page.tsx" 102 import { Suspense } from 'react' 103 104 async function LatestPosts() { 105 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/posts') 106 const posts = await data.json() 107 return ( 108
    109 {posts.map((post) => ( 110
  • {post.title}
    • 111 ))} 112
113 ) 114 } 115 116 export default function Page() { 117 return ( 118 <> 119

My Blog

120 Loading posts...

}> 121 122 123 124 ) 125 } 126 ``` 127 128 The fallback (`

Loading posts...

`) is included in the static shell, while the component's content streams in at request time. 129 130 `` provides a fallback UI while async work completes, but it does not itself opt a component into dynamic rendering. If a component only performs synchronous work, it will complete during prerendering regardless of whether it is wrapped in ``. 131 132 ## Working with runtime APIs 133 134 Runtime APIs require information that is only available when a user makes a request. These include: 135 136 - [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) - User's cookie data 137 - [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) - Request headers 138 - [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) - URL query parameters 139 - [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional) - Dynamic route parameters (unless at least one sample is provided via [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params)). 140 141 Components that access runtime APIs should be wrapped in ``: 142 143 ```tsx filename="page.tsx" 144 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 145 import { Suspense } from 'react' 146 147 async function UserGreeting() { 148 const cookieStore = await cookies() 149 const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')?.value || 'light' 150 return

Your theme: {theme}

151 } 152 153 export default function Page() { 154 return ( 155 <> 156

Dashboard

157 Loading...

}> 158 159 160 161 ) 162 } 163 ``` 164 165 ### Passing runtime values to cached functions 166 167 You can extract values from runtime APIs and pass them as arguments to cached functions: 168 169 ```tsx filename="app/profile/page.tsx" 170 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 171 import { Suspense } from 'react' 172 173 export default function Page() { 174 return ( 175 Loading...}> 176 177 178 ) 179 } 180 181 // Component (not cached) reads runtime data 182 async function ProfileContent() { 183 const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value 184 return 185 } 186 187 // Cached component receives extracted value as a prop 188 async function CachedContent({ sessionId }: { sessionId: string }) { 189 'use cache' 190 // sessionId becomes part of the cache key 191 const data = await fetchUserData(sessionId) 192 return
{data}
193 } 194 ``` 195 196 At request time, `CachedContent` executes if no matching cache entry is found, and stores the result for future requests with the same `sessionId`. 197 198 By default, `use cache` stores entries [in-memory](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#runtime-caching-considerations). In serverless environments where memory doesn't persist across requests, `CachedContent` may re-evaluate on every request. Consider [`'use cache: remote'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) for durable, shared caching. 199 200 ## Working with non-deterministic operations 201 202 Operations like `Math.random()`, `Date.now()`, or `crypto.randomUUID()` produce different values each time they execute. See [Route Handlers with Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers#with-cache-components) for details. 44 45 ## Usage 46 47 The [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive caches the return value of async functions and components.
